Item 1 (blocking) is fixed. I reproduced it on round 1 first, with the real CLI on uv 0.11.14, 0.11.19 and 0.12.23. uv first discovers a PROJECT: the nearest pyproject.toml, or its workspace root. It then reads configuration from that root, so an ancestor pyproject.toml with [project] took the search past the uv.toml sentinel. I confirmed this in uv's source (lib.rs: Workspace::discover, then FilesystemOptions::find), which is the same in 0.11.14 and 0.12.23.

I chose the mechanism by measurement: ten ancestor shapes x five candidates x user pin and system pin, on all three uv versions, byte-identical, no warnings.
- uv.toml only (round 1): read the ancestor in 4 of 10 shapes
- pyproject.toml only: 9 of 10
- bare directory: 9 of 10
- --no-config: read nothing, but also lost the user and system pins. --config-file holds only one file, which uv then reads alone. --project only says where discovery starts.
- uv.toml plus a comment-only pyproject.toml (no [project], no [tool.uv]): read no ancestor in any shape and kept both pins.

So installer-cwd now holds those two aelix files. Each is rewritten (unlinked, then written, never through a link) whenever its text differs.

Item 2 is fixed. _uv_project_config / _uv_settings_root now model uv's discovery:
- an explicit workspace root
- a [project] joins a workspace above it when that workspace's members include it and its exclude does not
- no [project], managed=false, an unparsable file or a nameless [project] all mean the search starts at the cwd
- after that, the first uv.toml or [tool.uv] pyproject from that root upward wins

_uv_config_files now also covers the user file per platform (%APPDATA% on Windows), the system file, UV_NO_CONFIG, and UV_CONFIG_FILE read alone.

blocking.title: ADR-0251 section 11 and the commit message say M6 is equivalent, but it is not: a duck-typed registry's hit loses its headers under M6 and no row goes red
blocking.detail: Both the ADR sabotage table (M6 row) and REVIEW ROUND 2 in the message say M6 (the launch's own _openrouter_base call drops headers) is equivalent. blocking.title: A relative UV_CONFIG_FILE=uv.toml silently reads aelix's empty uv.toml, and the model reads a different file, so both org pins are dropped while the ADR says uv fails loudly
blocking.detail: In a catalog install or update, a relative UV_CONFIG_FILE is resolved in the uv child's cwd, which is installer-cwd. When it names uv.toml (or ./uv.toml, and pyproject.toml the same way), it lands on aelix's own empty file, so uv raises no error. _uv_config_files instead returns the relative path unchanged, and _read_uv_config_table opens it against aelix's process cwd, which is the user's directory. So _uv_has_own_index_config reads a file the uv child never reads, finds index keys there, and turns the pip.conf / PIP_INDEX_URL translation off. Result: neither the uv.toml pin nor the pip org pin applies. The catalog name resolves on uv's default index, and the consent block shows no index line while it says 'your user-level uv.toml and UV_* still apply'. This is the silent index switch ADR-0200 exists to prevent. Three claims are false: ADR-0255 sec 15 known limits ('uv fails on the missing file, nothing is redirected', and its own example is UV_CONFIG_FILE=uv.toml), ADR-0200 sec 12 ('_uv_config_files returns what uv reads from there'), and the commit message ('a file uv never read no longer switches the pip.conf translation off'). The trigger is narrow (a relative UV_CONFIG_FILE named uv.toml or pyproject.toml); other names fail loudly as documented. Small fix: in _uv_config_files, join a relative UV_CONFIG_FILE onto cwd (the child's), so the model reads what uv reads. Do not anchor it at the user's cwd, because that re-opens #392 for anyone with UV_CONFIG_FILE=uv.toml set globally. Optionally refuse or warn on a relative one for these installs. Correct both ADR sentences and the message, and add a test row.
blocking.evidence: Real CLI on uv 0.11.14, 0.11.19 and 0.12.23 (.omc/probes/392-live/r2verify/relenv.txt). For a catalog install, UV_CONFIG_FILE=uv.toml and ./uv.toml gave rc=1 'local-ext was not found in the cache' (the default-index path) with no 'failed to open' line. pinned.toml gave rc=2 'failed to open file'. UV_FIND_LINKS=./w gave rc=2 'Failed to read --find-links directory .../installer-cwd/w'. A typed install got the pin. relcfg-model.txt (uv 0.12.23, PIP_INDEX_URL=org-pip, cwd uv.toml with index-url): without UV_CONFIG_FILE the consent block prints '-> UV_INDEX_URL=https://org-pip...'. With UV_CONFIG_FILE=uv.toml that line is gone, and 'uv -v' run in installer-cwd prints 'Using configuration file: uv.toml' (aelix's empty file).
